utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. At the close of the proceedings yesterday, I believe I finished my questions of this witness with one minor housekeeping matter which I had not attended to and that was the tendering of the book and the copy as an exhibit, and I would ask the Court for that, and that's the only thing that I believe I've left to do with this witness at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. May we have a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Should the photocopy be marked as 23A just in case, because not everybody has a copy of the entire book?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the practice?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's useful to have. 23A.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Greaves:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Arifagic, can you help me, please, about your involvement in any way before the war in politics? Were you so involved?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been involved since the war?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did your national service in the JNA around 1979, 1980, sometime around there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what branch of the military were you involved in during your service?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the infantry branch and special sabotage units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- after completing your national service, did you go on to the JNA reserve, and did you keep up that commitment?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were released from Trnopolje in October 1992, did you subsequently serve in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I -- in October of the same year, I left for Norway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you help us about this, please: Do you have any sort of relationship or have you ever had with the intelligence and security services of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to late 1991 and early 1992, at that period, Croats and Muslims started to refuse to answer call-up to the JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Croats and Muslims in the Prijedor area refused to go to the call-up in order not to go to the war in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that pretty well universal amongst Croatian and Muslim men, that they didn't answer the call-up?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was universally accepted, and from what I knew, there was a direction from the government in Sarajevo that we did not need to go to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of not answering the call-up and because of desertions from the JNA, was that the cause that the JNA became dominated by Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the reason was that it had become the Serb army, but I would not call a desertion a refusal to join a certain army to go and carry out an aggression against another country. I don't think that that is desertion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At around that time, you observed, did you not, a build-up of JNA troops in the Prijedor area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that those were either in part or, in fact, wholly troops who were being re-deployed from Croatia as a result of the withdrawal of the JNA from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that, because I was not interested in the military and political affairs. What I could see were military columns that were moving through, and I knew that this was not an usual phenomenon in our area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, military preparations in the Prijedor area were not just carried out only by Serbs, were they?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the Muslims were organising themselves militarily, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That organisation boiled down exclusively to the protection of the areas where we lived. If you referring to an organisation as something that was set up in order to carry out an aggression, then there was no such organisation, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the 31st of April, 1992, guns were being brought into Muslim areas, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that there were weapons in that period, because all sides were bringing them in, and if they were brought in, that was done by the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, hand-held antitank weapons for the use of infantry, like the Zolja, that was the sort of thing that was being brought in, wasn't it, by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they had them, then they could only have bought it from the Yugoslav People's Army. They could not have bought it from any other source.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not being brought in from abroad, the international arms market? Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, Kozarac was completely blocked, so I don't know where it could have come from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about the period before April, 1992, Mr. Arifagic. It's right, isn't it, that there were also extra food supplies were brought into the Kozarac area? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear about that, and I was busy building my family home. Perhaps for your information, just 20 days before the aggression, I had completed it, and then 20 days later, it burned down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you hear of extra sanitary and medical supplies being brought into the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the Crisis Staff formed in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly. I don't even know who the members were. I know what people were saying, that this, the Crisis Staff, did exist and that Kozarac should be organised exclusively as defence, that we should not touch anyone, that we would try to negotiate with Prijedor in order to avoid the conflict. Our interest in any event was to prevent conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you didn't know who they were. At one stage, when you were guarding the post at Balte, you were able to communicate with the Crisis Staff. Didn't you know whom you were communicating with, Mr. Arifagic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, that was on the eve of the attack, I contacted Captain Cirkin and Becir Medunjanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably were, given their positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of arms and ammunition were available to the people who were engaged in the military activities on the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, these were hunting weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many antitank weapons were there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the location where I was, there was nothing. In fact, tanks could not even reach this village where I was, Javori. This village is partly in a forest and it borders the Baltici village. We simply wanted to prevent anyone from entering it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that if tanks wanted to reach -- couldn't reach that area, there would be no point in having antitank weapons there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could not reach that village, but in other areas of -- along the Prijedor-Banja Luka stretch, they could approach.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would Your Honour just give me a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other preparations were made in the Kozarac area, such as Zemunica, which are underground shelters; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People were doing that on their own initiative in case of shelling so that they could protect themselves and their own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they also prepared on the instructions of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that most part of that was done on people's own initiatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of uniform did you have when you were guarding the village?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean personally myself?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You and your fellow Muslims who were engaged in this activity?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area where I was, people were mostly wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say what role the Crisis Staff played in Kozarac exactly?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- according to me, this is my opinion, I think that they were involved in the negotiations with the people in Prijedor in order to attempt to prevent any conflict between people in Kozarac, in other words so that we do not be attacked and that we prevent the outbreak of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would have been obvious, would it not, by early May, 1992, to anyone carrying out any sort of reconnaissance of Kozarac, that there was a substantial number of armed men in the area?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what men you're referring to, if you're talking in general, there was a huge number of men who were JNA men, and they were billeted at Benko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking, Mr. Arifagic, about people on the Muslim side. In due course, when Kozarac was attacked by the Muslims, you were able to muster some 750 men to do that. It must have been obvious, mustn't it, by May, 1992, that there were a substantial number of Muslim men armed and ready to take military action? That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a military action, and it wasn't 750 men. If we had 750 men ready for a military action, everything would have been different. So this was -- all it was was men trying to protect their families. At that time, those who had small children and wives in the Kozarac area had to do something in order to try to protect them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How many men were there, Mr. Arifagic? You said it wasn't 750 men. How many men were there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know directly what the gentleman is referring to. Kozarac had 24.000 inhabitants. People were on duty in -- around their area. I don't know what the gentleman is referring to, to whom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Arifagic, in your statement that you made to the Office of the Prosecutor in October 1994, you said that in respect of mounting a fresh attack, "We divided into three groups of about 250 people in each group." That makes 750. Where did all those people come from?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were groups of men who managed to gather at Mount Kozara after the fall of Kozarac after meeting with Captain Cirkin and Becir Medunjanin. Men were talking about what to do. Some of them wanted to cross Mount Kozara and going to Croatia, and for the most part, these were men who were civilians. One part of the men decided that a fresh attempt should be made to take control of the town, and the number of people who took part in the attack on Kozarac was a much, much smaller number. And from what I know, nothing was done. Nothing was accomplished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come back to that in a moment. The first fighting which occurred was on the 24th of May, 1992, around Donji Garevci; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, we seem to be spending a considerable amount of time on the issue of the armed conflict. I understand that it's an issue that the Prosecution has to prove, but we don't have to prove as to who started it. I don't believe who started it is relevant. So my -- are my friends now belatedly admitting that there is an armed -- that was an armed conflict? Because if so, I think these questions are becoming irrelevant, especially if we get to the issue of who seems to be responsible for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think it may be relevant to the kind of Defence Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 that's being mounted. Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It's also relevant, in our submission, to the legitimacy of detaining people of military age during an armed conflict, and it goes to the issue of genocide. The evidence in the case thus far is that people of military age were being detained and this is the reason why they were being detained. Not genocide, this reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Arifagic, I asked you about the initial outbreak of fighting on the 24th of May, 1992. Is it correct that that occurred near Donji Garevci?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the direction of Donji Garevci and Orlovci, but what it was, it was an attack on -- on -- from the Serb part. The shells started falling. It wasn't a direct confrontation, conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's right, in due course, that you were able to hear from the radio that Serbs were approaching a checkpoint at Jakupovici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This took place later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the orders were then given to attack the tanks without further warning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Captain Cirkin issued that because people who were in the checkpoint at Jakupovici were there because they were not going anywhere. They were not attacking the tanks or the military that were coming. The tanks and the troops were probably coming to attack and destroy the village, so the people were defending themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that we go quite shortly through this, it's right, isn't it, that over a period of about three or four days there was substantial amount of fighting in the Kozarac area? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't call it fighting. It was an advance of the Serb troops, and we were simply withdrawing towards the centre of Kozarac. And after these men gathered in the centre of Kozarac, they surrendered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just help us about this, please. The 750 people of whom we have talked, those people all took part in an attack on Kozarac, did they not?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all of them. It was a group of 750 men who gathered at the foothills of Mount Kozara, but the number of those who took part in the attack was much smaller. And it wasn't an attack. When the tanks opened fire, they immediately withdrew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'd like to establish is that Kozarac having been taken by the Serbs, there was an agreement amongst those of you who had got away to carry out a counter-attack; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're trying to say about the agreement to carry out a counter-attack. We tried to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Arifagic, we will get on more quickly -- don't bother to argue with counsel. Don't bother to argue with counsel. But that appears to have been your evidence. And, Mr. Greaves, it is sometimes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- not really worth it to go over what witnesses have said. It just leads to this sort of pointless argument. I think we've got the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Your Honour. I'm grateful to Your Honour for that piece of assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In due course, Mr. Arifagic, you were able to find out something about your father, that he'd been given some form of military certificate. What was the nature of that certificate?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I learnt later, when I found out the whereabouts of my family, that my father was in Trnopolje, I think that it was the Red Cross, that he had received a certificate and with this certificate he could leave to go to the village from where his wife was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, that that was a certificate given to him by the Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They issued it to him at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in particular, it was given to him because he was over the age which was considered to be military age. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were eventually detained, it's right, isn't it, that those who were detained at the same time as you were men of military age and capability; do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between your detention on the 14th of June, and your arrival at Omarska, you had property stolen from you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the property that was taken away from me, like the house?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. While you're on your way from being detained to Omarska, you --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, you're referring to -- yes, my watch, my gold chain, these things were taken away from me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all of your valuables were removed from you before you got to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Omarska that day, was it obvious that there was no room for you at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That explanation, I believe it was while we were still on the bus, simply the notice came, the rumour arrived, that there was no room for us. At that time we did not know where they would take us, but be that as it may, we were taken away to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the -- was it one bus or more than one bus that was in your convoy going to Omarska and then to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people on the bus in all?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think about 50 or maybe 60.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Keraterm and were placed in the room, how many people in all were in the room?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say about 250, 300 at that particular moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the course of your stay in Keraterm, what was the maximum number, as far as you could ascertain, of people detained in all the facility?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speak about Room 2. I think the largest number was 500, 550 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly, concerning the beating after your arrival, it's right, isn't it, that it was soldiers, i.e., military people, who were doing that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the focus of their dislike of you was the suggestion that you were Green Berets, in other words, members of the Muslim special forces?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if Green Berets are Muslim forces, but that was the reason for them to beat me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Concerning the person who you were told was named Sikirica, you told us yesterday that you had seen him before the war. Can you help us as to this? Why did you say, when you made your statement in 1994 to the Office of the Prosecutor, "I had only ever seen him in the camp"?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in the camp, but I also used to see him before the war. He'd be passing by in the street and I simply knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that being so, why did you say, "I had only ever seen him in the camp," when you gave your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor two years after these events?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I did say that, but I do remember seeing that man before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to recall now who it was who told you that his name was Sikirica?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was men who were in dormitory 2. It was mostly people from Baska, from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able now to recall when it was you first saw the man you described as Dusko Sikirica when you got to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I can remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in due course, you were taken to the hospital. It's right, isn't it, that the man Dosen was involved in those arrangements for sending you to hospital?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I think one has to be realistic. He is the only one I can thank that I did go to hospital and thus survived. Of course, it was unfortunate that Zigic was on the -- in the same vehicle, but it is he that I have to thank for sending me there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's right also, is it not, that Dosen asked you who it was who had beaten you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a pretty fair idea of who it was, at least one of those who had been involved in beating you, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Despite knowing who it was, you lied to Dosen and said you did not know who it was who had beaten you, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They -- no, I did not lie. I could have said it but in a camp, when you are beaten, I think it's best to keep silent, and he's very well aware of that and we understand one another. That is how it was. I simply shrugged my shoulders and he helped me go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in the absence of telling him who it was, he could not take any steps against the person who had done it to you, could he?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. Perhaps I could have said who that was and then that same day or that night, I could have been then taken out and -- so it was a golden rule, just keep silent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the hospital, it's right, isn't it, that there was a Muslim doctor on duty?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. As we were in the waiting room at the entrance to the hospital, he approached us and he talked with us, with that group of camp inmates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it would seem, would it not, from that, that not all Muslims had been dismissed from their posts in the services available in the Prijedor area; would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the area of Prijedor. What I can say is that at that moment, that man who was a Muslim was in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to the beating of Emsud Bahonjic, it's right, isn't it that Zigic had made the specific allegation about him that he was the sniper who tried to kill a relation of Zigic's; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was one of the reasons why Zigic got involved in beating Emsud Bahonjic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was his -- that was -- he said that that was why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it also be right that the people from -- who had been detained from Kozarac were singled out because of the resistance which had taken place at Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that, and I cannot say whether that was the reason, but people from Kozarac were, on the whole, beaten and mistreated more than others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a second group taken to hospital. Were there any other groups whilst you were in Keraterm who were taken to hospital for treatment, apart from the two groups that you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think on yet another occasion, a doctor came and examined some people, but it was eight or nine years ago, so I can't really remember everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now, please, if you will, to the beating and killing of Drago Tokmadzic, would you accept that the reason that he was singled out was because he was an active police officer from Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that we were already in a camp for some time, and I can say what Drago told me when they were brought to Room 2, that they had signed the loyalty to the Republika Srpska in the Ministry of the Interior, that they were performing their duties as usual, but that on that particular day there they had been disarmed and brought to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've described someone else who was beaten as having the name Fikret, at about the same time. Do you think you may have mistaken the name of Fikret and, in fact, it was somebody called Esad Islamovic, who was also a policeman from Ljubija?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think so. I know that they were brought together, that they were beaten together, that Drago did not come back, and that man's name, I think, is Fikret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father arrived at Keraterm, and it's right, isn't it, that before he had -- before his arrival, he had been ill-treated? In other words, the ill-treatment took place outside the camp?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was maltreated as he was being brought to the camp. And perhaps we can now go back to what you asserted earlier. At the time when Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 he was arrested in that village, when he got there with the certificate, he showed the certificate, but the soldier just tore it up, said, "This is not worth anything," and that is how he ended. So that this certificate for men who were not militarily active did not help him. He was beaten again. He spent 15 days in the camp, and he was then taken back to Trnopolje, that is, to the very same place where this certificate had been issued to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were interrogated on the 10th of July, 1992, and when you were taken for your interrogation, you were taken, I think, by Kajin's younger brother; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we gather from that that the role of the guards at Keraterm was simply to escort detainees from the rooms downstairs, upstairs to the rooms where interviews were taking place?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Kajin Jr.'s role was to take me there and escort me, but the role of other guards was to guard us, to watch us round the clock; that is, we were under their control and command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I put the question badly, and I apologise for so doing. In relation to the interrogations which were taking place upstairs, Mr. Arifagic, and the guards who were at Keraterm, the guards did not take part in the interrogations, did they?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the room that we were taken to, they did not, at least not in my case. The man who interrogated me was someone whom I had never seen before, whom I never saw in the compound among the guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were interviewed just by one person. Did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By sight perhaps, but no particulars. He interrogated me and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was interested, was he not, in particular in your -- whether you had taken part in politics before the war and whether you'd taken part in fighting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to the man Cupo Banovic, it's right, isn't it, that he spent a lot of time extorting money from prisoners? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was another guard, Sahadzija, who was engaged in stealing watches from prisoners?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't stealing them. He only demanded that watches be turned over to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, whether it's stealing or turning them over, he ended up with prisoners' watches; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Room 3 incident, Mr. Arifagic, at some stage you heard an order for people to lie down. It's right, isn't it, that you don't know who issued that order?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were locked in the room and the order came at that moment. I did not know who the order came from, but whatever the case, we were ordered to lie down and not to move and to keep silent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- after the incident, the following day there were people who came to the camp, one of whom was Simo Drljaca. It's right, isn't it, that he was a well-known figure in Prijedor? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, you had known him before the war as a former communist who was involved in the police service?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him by sight. That was a household name because he was very active politically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was an older man with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes. I think there was a man with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that someone you had seen on a regular basis in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Dusko Sikirica was accompanying him, but the older man who was with him, he was not somebody that I normally saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't normally see him but you did see him on occasion before that day?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That man, you mean, that elderly man who was -- no, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I suggest to you, and if you're able to assist us with this, do so, that that older man's name was Zivko Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That name tells me nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The older man, was he someone who you saw on any occasion giving orders in the camp?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were the -- Simo Drljaca and this older man, how were they dressed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Drljaca was in, well, what we call police camouflage uniform, which is a combat uniform, the one that you use in war. The other one was in a military uniform. I can't remember that exactly. But Simo Drljaca was wearing a blue camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that you considered that the conditions at the camp were totally chaotic, completely chaotic around that time? That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot -- I cannot say if they were chaotic. I do not know what normal conditions in a camp are. I do not know what normal conditions are like, and are camps and camp conditions something normal? I wouldn't call it chaotic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In October 1994, when you made your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, that is precisely how you described the conditions at that time. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Duca Knezevic, of whom you are aware, he was not a guard at the camp, was he?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not. At least I do not think so, but he used to come there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Zoran Zigic also, although he may have been a guard at one time, ceased to be a guard but continued to come after that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Room 3 killings, according to what you were told by Kajin, was a combination of retaliation for what had happened in World War II and the killing of Serb troops in Hambarine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just return very briefly to the day after the first incident in Room 3? Do you know somebody called Dule Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think -- no. I don't know. I mean, it vaguely rings a bell. I think the man was with the traffic police, but I'm really not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can suggest to you that he was with Simo Drljaca on the day that that person was at the camp, can you help us about that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you gave evidence to the Tribunal in 1996, you presumably took an oath, as you did on this occasion, to tell the truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that you told them on that occasion, the Tribunal on that occasion, that the Keraterm camp was guarded by Serb guards who you thought were from paramilitary units; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it not right that you told the Tribunal on that occasion that those people were all the time under the orders of people who wore military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that. What I know is only what I could see around me, and I know that men who guarded us determined our life, but who issued orders to whom, I could not know that, being in the camp. Nor did we have any information in that respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you accept that that, what I have just read out to you, is what you told the Trial Chamber on the 8th of August, 1996, Mr. Arifagic? They were all the time under the orders of people who wore military uniform -- uniforms? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just returning briefly to two matters, please. It's right, isn't it, that the most dangerous period of time for prisoners in the camp was at night-time?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people who were most feared were Duca Knezevic, Zoran Zigic, and Cupo Banovic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The book from which you garnered names of members of your family, that's a book that you brought and gave to Mr. Ryneveld?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I bought that book because that book can be bought in Bosnia in almost every bookshop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was you who gave it to the Prosecution rather than the Prosecution seeking it from you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I showed it to them, but he had a book, and I suppose he came by it himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it relate only to people in the Prijedor area or is it a book which deals with all of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's a book which I believe was published by the association of wives and mothers who lost their men, and I think it is a book of people who were identified, people who are reported as missing, and it covers by and large the area of the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it in fact drawn from a register of people who are missing?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say yes or no because I did not publish it, so I do not know what the sources were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the names that you've picked out in highlighter in the lists that we have got, ten of them have no date of disappearance. Would you accept that? Disappearance or death?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. I mean, they are registered as missing but there is no date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of the names again that you highlighted, none of those people was in Keraterm, were they?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, were you aware in Keraterm of an individual called Bajazit Jakupovic, who was a pilot?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember him. He was in my dormitory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he subsequently transferred to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was taken to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would Your Honour just give me a moment?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as Bajazit Jakupovic was concerned, did you hear from anybody what had happened to him at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, your stay in Trnopolje, did you ever see Dusko Sikirica there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I remember seeing him. I didn't. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Greaves. Mr. Petrovic? Cross-examined by Mr. Petrovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said that you returned to Kozarac in December, 1991. Why did you come back home at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was normal to come back in this period. I was involved in building my family home and I had spent a number of -- a period of time in our -- the construction projects abroad, in Africa. I came back to finish the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before that you worked in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you finish the job in Croatia and this is why you came back, or was it for family reasons?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was for family reasons. I took a leave of absence because I used to work six months at a time without a break and so I took time off to finish the family house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned on several occasions an oath of loyalty to the new authorities?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This oath of loyalty, was this something that was asked individually of people of Muslim ethnic background or was it for the whole area?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was for the -- all of -- the whole of Kozarac. I think that people who were in leading positions in police and civilian authorities, that they -- they were asked to say that they were loyal to the Serb authorities in Prijedor. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it perhaps what was asked of the political leaders in Prijedor also to surrender weapons which they had?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was a condition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can agree that what was really implied by loyalty, the surrender of weapons that people had with them?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what loyalty comprised of, but one of the conditions was that when these people -- when people who were -- who had been wounded were supposed to be taken to the Prijedor hospital, to be treated, that was one of the conditions made to Becir Medunjanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement to the Tribunal in 1994, you said that seven days before the attack on Kozarac, a barricade had been erected at Kozarusa; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the last checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This checkpoint was set up by the inhabitants of Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that they did. Before that, a control checkpoint had been erected at Orlovci so our access to Piro had been cut off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there -- I need to go a little bit slower because of the interpreters. Was there a checkpoint at the entrance of Kozarac, that is coming from the main road?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe so. I think that this was at Jakupovic and at Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The checkpoint at Kozarusa was manned by locals from Kozarusa who were of Muslim ethnic background and they were organised in Territorial Defence or something like that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at that checkpoint, but I assumed that these were people who lived in Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were people of Muslim ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we agree that the main highway between Prijedor and Banja Luka passes through Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that in fact the Prijedor -- the area of Prijedor, by setting up of this checkpoint, had been cut off from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the checkpoint at Orlovci had been set up even earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement you also said that after the change of power in Prijedor, the police in Kozarac, that is before the takeover, the police was composed of both Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you said that after the takeover of power, the Serb members of the police left their duties in Kozarac. Why did this happen?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the takeover of power, because Kozarac at that time did not declare loyalty, from what I know they simply did not show up at work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why? Do you have any idea about why they did not -- stopped coming to work?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, the commander of police in Kozarac was a Serb. Why they stopped coming to work, why only Muslims remained in the police force, and some Croats, that ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You served in a special unit in Paunci during your national service, so I assume that you know something about the military structure and the organisation of units starting with the squad, platoon, company, and so on. Can you tell us, how was the defence of Kozarac organised in that respect? Were you divided into squads, platoons, companies?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such organisation. The organisation consisted simply of the locals from certain village forming guards and checkpoints. In other words, the outside perimeter of Kozarac was protected so that there would be no incursions or no attempts made on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement from 1994, you said that as a response to the takeover of power in Prijedor, guards were set up facing the villages, the Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In these first days after the takeover of power in Prijedor, as far as I understand, there were no conflicts in that area?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, during your examination-in-chief, you said that six men were killed by a shell which -- who were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The six men -- were these six men involved in the defence of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, they were in this village. In other words, there was a large group of locals there, and at that point when they were killed, that was the very beginning of the attack. They were at their guard posts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Senad Cirkin. Later on during your stay -- during your imprisonment in Keraterm did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once. I think he was brought in at nightfall and the next day he was led away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he treated at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was brought in. I cannot recall exactly where he was put, in which room. I think that one of the guards came and called the captain, asking him to come out and eat, and he refused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was not mistreated or beaten from what you know?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know. He was not in my room, so I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Medunjanin also brought in to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you provided us with a sketch which you had drawn, and were -- was it possible to enter Keraterm on the back side of Keraterm where --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware that there was any gate and entrance there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned that at one point, bars were placed on the doors of the room where you were.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were they put there, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion was - and I think that I share that opinion with other men from Room 2 - it happened often that Zigic would come in at night. He would drive in with Mercedes, and he would drive in this car in the room itself. So people would jump up and try to go to the back of the room. And because of these frequent visits, I explained that this door, and this was a metal door -- these bars were placed also, they said, so that we would have more air during the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would I be wrong in saying that these bars were placed in order to protect you from the night visitors and, on the other hand, to allow you to have more air?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the explanation. Probably what we all agreed on was that we had more air.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Kajin getting into a conflict with Zigic who was coming and mistreating people?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You shook your head, but I need a verbal answer from you.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer was, "No."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bars were placed there after your arrival at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until then there was a full metal door there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you could not see outside through that door?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not when they were closed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that the majority of the guards, during the day, stood around the weigh hut. Did that mean that they did not have specific sentry posts, guard posts, but that they, rather, grouped or walked about without any particular order?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- apart from those guards who were at machine-gun nests, most of the guards spent their time around and inside that hut, from what we could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you mentioned the height of the room where you were, and you said that it was about two, two and a half metres high.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two and a half, three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But then you said it could be higher because a trailer truck could come in.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was about three metres high, and from what I know, these trucks were two metres twenty high, so I think that this kind of truck could have entered this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to please show the witness Prosecution Exhibit number 21, which is the sketch provided by the witness. Can the exhibit please be placed on the ELMO so that everybody would be able to follow my questions to the witness as I ask him to explain certain details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this sketch, you marked the rooms. You placed them in order and used -- in your sketch, we see that the toilet is between Rooms 3 and 4.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how I drew it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could -- would you accept that the arrangement of rooms was a bit different?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This was done four years after my stay in Keraterm, so I did it to the best of my recollection. I drew what I remembered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember - and it is not represented in the sketch - that in front of Room 1 there was a kiosk where the guards were staying?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it did exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that kiosk look, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It may have been like a newspaper,like a news stand type of kiosk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was such a kiosk also near the gate where you said that it was a gate for pedestrians and vehicles?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the grassy area in front of Rooms 3 and 4, were there poles on which the floodlights were mounted?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that these lights virtually did not work?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in -- for the most part they did not, but there were nights when it did work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When lights were not on, you could not see clearly from the room where you were what was going on in the other parts -- in the areas around?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you could.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We don't need the sketch any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, when you mentioned men who were in Room 2 where you had spent your detention, you said that there were men from Puharska, then later on from Ljubija, also from Kozarac. Can we conclude that, in fact, there were men from all different areas of Prijedor? Were there also people from Brdo?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very few, but probably there were some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean, in fact, that men were not grouped by room, at the time when you had come, based on what area of the municipality they were coming from but on some other principle? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think at that time. I don't know what the organisation was, but not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember that shortly after -- that when you arrived, at first there were two shifts and then the organisation, as you knew it, was established?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I don't know how many shifts there were and what the organisation was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many hours was one shift?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that these guard shifts changed at 7.00 in the morning and 7.00 in the evening and then it rotated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would mean that it lasted for about 12 hours each?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you mentioned a person who beat you. You said that his name was Milan and that he was working at the Oslobodenje newsstand.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you had noticed as much as you could, given that you were badly beaten, that he was wearing white belt, such as the military police members were wearing?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he had them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we conclude, then, that since he had such a uniform, that he was a member of the military police?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say to which units he belonged. He just had them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him later at Keraterm, this guard, Milan?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This happened at the very beginning?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This happened the very night I was brought to the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we conclude that, then, he was not a guard at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in any event, did you not see him after that incident?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When asked by my learned friend, Mr. Greaves, you confirmed that the conditions in the camp were chaotic and there was lack of organisation. Is this very different from the order and organisation, let's say, in the unit in the army when you served?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It differed very much from the regular organisation of the JNA, and it was normal, but because this was a camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that after your first beating, Kajin's shift came on duty that next morning?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During the night, that is before the morning, I was bleeding all night. I was informed, I think, that it was the men from Puharska who told me that Kajin and his shift would come on duty and that he was a good guy and that I should try to talk to him, that he may be able to help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that you were bleeding profusely and that your life was in danger?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was bleeding a lot. I had been beaten severely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The assistance you were given was not adequate but the bleeding which you were suffering was stopped?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point in your statement, and I'm referring to the statement you gave in 1994, you said that Kajin was considered the best commander in Keraterm. Why? What -- why did people think so?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you perhaps my own opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is exactly what I'm asking you, your own opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My personal opinion was because personally he never mistreated me, he never beat me. And now, whether he could prevent others from mistreating me and beating me, that is another issue, but he personally never beat me, never mistreated me, and he was the only man with whom I established contact in the camp and whom I -- with whom -- whom I had a human contact. He allowed me to go to the hospital. And also I want to explain that the night that he was in front of the room, the words that he said perhaps agreed with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that. But we were talking about the chaos reigning in the camp, with this chaos and -- could it be that due to this chaos and lack of order, you did not tell Kajin who it was that beat you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe specifically, I perhaps could not tell him I was beaten by such and such a person and then expect him to help me. That was the golden rule.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the rule of the strongest and the most bestial that reigned, the person who wanted to do something would be able to do it and he would not have been able to prevent them and do anything about it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his position and the amount of power he had, but I know that those who carried weapons and those who were guarding us could do whatever they want with us, if we were not protected, if there was nobody around to protect us, nobody could do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that if Kajin were present, that he would always try to prevent such occurrences?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How well did you know Kajin before the war? You said that you knew him in passing?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we knew each other from passing. I knew his brother. I knew him better, because we both went to the same technical secondary school. But these were meetings in town. I went to this town for four years to go to school, so I knew a number of people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what I understand, you never socialised with Kajin before the war because you were not the same age group, you were not peers, so your acquaintance with him was superficial?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was just meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My correction. My colleague has just pointed something out to me. Am I wrong in saying that I am -- you are agreeing with me that Kajin tried to prevent things?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think my question to you was wrong. What you're trying to tell us was that Kajin did try to prevent these incidents?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- what I'm trying to say is when Kajin was in the camp, and I'm only talking in my own name, at that time when he was there, there was no mistreatment of people, if he was at his post, if he was with his guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see anyone -- at any time that he ordered anyone to mistreat someone?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were talking about visitors to the camp, like Zigic and Duca. Were these people who were bullies and who were even prepared to shoot at Serbs in order to gain access to people whom they want to mistreat? Was that the impression you gained from --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were prepared to shoot at Serbs, but Zigic was also bully before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that before the war, he had been convicted of murder?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but he had a powerful family that protected him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a van that was taking you to the hospital, the driver was trying to prevent Zigic were taking out aggression on you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Had it not been for him, I think that we would not have fared well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That day, that was the 15th of June, when you were taken to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that in fact that morning, Kajin sent those men to the hospital, including you, and that Zigic was so powerful that he was able to have the men brought back without them having been treated?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the hospital, what happened was what he demanded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the doctors in the hospital were obeying Zigic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Emsud was brought back without actually getting any help because Zigic told the doctor to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, in your examination-in-chief, you said that two policemen, Fikret and Drago, were brought to Room 2?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who had called -- who called them out to -- from Room 2 when they were beaten?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who it was, but Fikret later told us that the Banovic brothers were there in the group of men who beat them when they were brought out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did Fikret come back to the room?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that somebody had come to the gate, one of the guard -- commanders of the guard, and this is how he was able to go back to the room. And I think that the next day he was taken to the hospital or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he carried into the room or did he go in on his own power?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any argument and quarrel between the ones that you assumed were beating him and the person who you -- who arrived in the compound?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could hear screams from outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago that probably one of the commanders came to Keraterm. Did you hear any kind of conversation, any kind of argument?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall. I did not hear it, but I believe that that was the reason -- actually, I think that Fikret actually pointed out that somebody had come in, and this is the reason why he was still alive and why he had been brought back to the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, we are at the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that was exactly what I was about to suggest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Arifagic, we take a break for half an hour. We return at 11.30. During the break, you're not to discuss your evidence with anyone, including members of the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you're continuing with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to go back briefly to the conditions in the room that you were in. You mentioned in your statement that there was a barrel which was brought in after your arrival and which you used to relieve yourselves overnight.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that barrel brought in?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That barrel was brought in so that overnight people could relieve themselves so as not to have to go out to the lavatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the usher to help me show a document that I have here, to show it to the witness. It is the protocol of the hospital in Prijedor. [In English] I have a copy for Their Honours, and I've already gave that to the -- already gave to the Prosecution. Just for Their Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 Honours. [Interpretation] I apologise to the Court for having only the English translation. We are really doing our best to have it also translated into the other working language of the Tribunal. As soon as this is done, we shall submit that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Arifagic, I should like to ask you -- I believe it is on page 2 of this protocol, under 3294, where your name figures and the date 15th of June. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. Will you look at the document that is in Bosnian, the document that you have in front of you. Do you see there on the second page, fourth column from above, do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the date 15th of June at the top of the column next to the first name. Next to the first name is the date 15th June and in the fourth column your name.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your name, your date of birth, and your place of residence?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we should like to tender this into evidence as this is the excerpt from the protocol of the Prijedor hospital for 15th of June, that is, the day when the witness was taken to the hospital and when some medical assistance was extended to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D2/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Arifagic, I should now like to ask you to look at those other names from the top of this page and the previous page. Do you know those people?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zijad Krivdic, Abaz Kulasic. I know those names. Emsud Bahonjic. These are more or less names that I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these persons who were brought to the hospital at the same time with you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. Some of those people were with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Usher. We shall not need this document any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like now to go back to the incident which you told us happened around the 1st of July, 1992, when you were beaten up, and you told us that it was a day when the food that you got was slightly better?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement to the Tribunal, you said it was on or about the 1st of July; you were not sure?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement you say, "The next morning, a doctor without an arm came and requested to examine wounded prisoners, if there were any, and Kajin told prisoners who had some injuries to go and see the doctor. I then heard that 28 prisoners were taken to the hospital because they had been beaten badly the night before. Some returned, some stayed in the hospital." Is that -- can you -- do you remember that event better, the event that you mentioned in your statement of 1994 now that I've reminded you of the statement? Do you have a better recollection of the event then?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I can infer, then, that that morning, after that beating, Kajin's shift took over the duty?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what Kajin's brother was called?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We called him Kajin Jr.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that you had talked with him when you came back from the interrogation and that he reminded you that you knew one another from the school days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd now like to go back briefly to the interrogation on the first floor of the administration building. In your statement you said that the interrogator told you, and I'm quoting you now your statement of 1994, "not to go out from Room 2 too often because I might be beaten."

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he told me not to come out of the room, but if I do go out, not to move forward too much because I had bandages on my head, and I had this white net there, so that I was really very conspicuous, and because of these head injuries, I kept this dressing on my head all the time, and he told me, "This is just too conspicuous so it's better for you to keep in the rear."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then does that mean that people who interrogated you were perfectly aware of horrible things happening in the dormitories and in front of them?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what he told me. What he was aware of, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea as to what was the relationship between interrogators and guards, who was superior to whom?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we could not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you about some individuals, some of whom come from your place, whether you know them and whether you saw them in Keraterm. Redzo Grabic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him.
