utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was there but I don't really ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in your room together with you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was in Room 2 but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ahmed Malkic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which room?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was Room 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mustafa Kapetanovic, called Muta?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fahrudin Mujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ismail Besic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I don't remember him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sajdo Besic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mujra Mahmuljin?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember him. He was in the same room as I, Room 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nedzad Mujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember him too. He was in Room 2 where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These few people that you say you know that were with you in the room, do you remember if they were at some point taken out together from that room that you were together in?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that Murat was taken out quite frequently and beaten but whether they were all taken out altogether, I don't really remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now ask you about a few incidents. Perhaps you will remember some of them, perhaps you will not, but if you do, then you will be able to help us, I hope. Are you aware that once, one of those visitors to the camp mounted the Zolja and wanted to fire at the room that you were in?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the van that you were transported to the hospital on that 15th of June, was it a blue and white van belonging to Kozara Putevi [phoen] which was always parked at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it driven by one of the guards who regularly turned up in the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who drove it, but the man who drove us there, I know him as a conductor who worked for Auto-transport, and I remember him from my secondary school days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you used to see that man as a guard around there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I should like to briefly touch upon the incident when Simo Drljaca and others came to Keraterm. Simo Drljaca promised you, if I understood you well, that the -- you would be better treated from then onward.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you understand him to mean that Drljaca, who promised that, also had the power and authority to see that that promise was kept and that he had some say in that place where you were?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we thought so since he was the man who was the chief of police at that time. But those were promises, and we had heard many promises before that and, nevertheless, things kept happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did he look like a man of authority?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I think that at that moment, he was a man who enjoys certain authority or who wielded certain authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that point in time, he looked there as somebody who was number one?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when he visited us and as he was speaking, as he was explaining something, I suppose he was the man who we listened to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to briefly remind you of the incident when Kajin came to your room. In your statement, you said that it happened two nights after the second rounds of fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also said that on that occasion, Kajin said that he disagreed with the Chetnik policy.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that he disagreed with the Chetnik policy, with the SDS policy, that he really did not want to see people tortured and mistreated. If somebody was guilty, then he should be brought to justice but -- rather than put people in front of a wall and have them shot. That is what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that he discarded the pistol that he had.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was hitting against the bars and did something with it. We could hear those sounds, but that was that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when that pistol was -- when he threw away that pistol, did he say then, "Kill me if you think that I'm responsible for anything"?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he weep as he said that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that you spoke with your fellow sufferers about what Kajin had said. What was their reaction to what they heard from him?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was a natural reaction of people. We were simply -- people heard that, and in the camp it was commented that, well ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you think that he was sincere when he said that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, but I think considering the state he was in, I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 believe, yes, he meant what he said, but what was the background of it all, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should also ask you a question or two to briefly go back to Room 2. Do you remember the man, the man who we saw on that photograph of Trnopolje who was shown here, that next to the door on a pallet there was sitting a young man who did not walk, who did not eat, and that Kajin then suggested that the man come out and walk around a little and eat something? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but I do remember that there was some instruction to take him out and help him walk around, to help him get some air. I remember, yes, that. Whether we were to take him out -- but, yes, I know there was this man, and we were told that we should take him out and help him walk around so that he could breathe some fresh air.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Kajin used to come to your room and talk with people who were detained there?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he would come to the door of the room, that is, at those times when we could be outside so that he would come there and communicate and talk with people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those were normal conversations between people from what you could see?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from what I could see, did he not beat anyone. Those were just normal conversations, people who knew him mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Vucicevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Arifagic, my name is Dusan Vucicevic. I'm an attorney from Chicago, and I represent Dragan Kolundzija. You have testified in direct and also when one of my learned friends at the Defence counsel table has asked you, you testified about your military experience while you served as a conscript in JNA, and you said that you were in the scout sabotage unit; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That unit was the sabotage unit of the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... had an additional training besides what was the basic infantry training?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. We did undergo some additional training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the length of that additional training and what did it consist of?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That training went on for about six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the length of your total service in JNA at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the total training was two months of infantry, basic infantry, plus six months of the special training; isn't that correct? I might be mistaken, but if you can help me on this.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the basic infantry was 2 months and 20 days, and after that we had some training which was also basically infantry training, and it was after that that we underwent supplementary training for sabotage units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it consisted of -- I don't know why is it important, but those sabotage units were mostly formed for the combat or for the -- to fight possible subversion units which came to Yugoslavia, and they were there to protect the general staff, and their main purpose was to defend and fight terrorist units and subversive units which made incursions into the then Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the checkpoint facing Serbian military units at Balte, were you in charge of that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have testified that you had a Motorola, a radio communication that usually police used, and you have talked to Captain Cirkin and Mr. Medunjanin. So is that -- that was in your possession, that you were responsible for it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was given that Motorola, and I could communicate with Becir Medunjanin and others. However, it wasn't a proper army or police Motorola. It was a contraption rather than a proper radio.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel be advised to mind breaks between questions and answers, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, the interpreters are asking you to observe the pause between question and answer. If you look on the transcript, you can see "[Previous translation continues] ..." at least twice, which means that there is an overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were the one who communicated with the superiors from that checkpoint; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though you didn't have a formal appointment or a rank but it was your responsibility to coordinate that point of the defence of Kozarac area; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not my duty. I was there like all the others. I was there standing guard, and it just so happened that I was the one who was given this Motorola in case we needed to communicate with someone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were basically one of the equals with the some special responsibilities just to communicate to superiors; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't their equal. Simply I had the possibility to communicate with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You were testifying about two checkpoints, major checkpoints, one in village of Jakupovici, and another is between Kozarusa and Orlovci; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Arifagic, I'm showing you a map that was -- that has already been admitted in evidence, and I would like you to mark - the pen is provided for you - to mark on that map exactly on that road where those checkpoints were. What I meant exactly, I mean what you can discern on that map where they were.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names of the villages are not here, but I shall try to put it tentatively somewhere along the road. [Witness marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it true that those two checkpoints that you just marked were located on and controlled traffic on the main road, the main thoroughfare between Prijedor and Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were there but they could not control any traffic at all because, before that, checkpoints had been set up at Orlovci and in the direction of Omarska so that ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's say if Serbian military wanted to pass from Banja Luka to Prijedor, they could pass through the Serbian checkpoint but they would be stopped by checkpoint that the Muslims of Kozarac have put right where you marked; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but one -- I have to point out that those checkpoints were put up on the eve of the attack on Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... is not important at this moment. Just it's important that they were there. And also the one, the marking that you put closer to Prijedor, right on the point between Orlovci and Kozarusa, that was also a checkpoint on a major road, the same road?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it reasonable to conclude that Yugoslav army, JNA, that was in Prijedor at that time, from the time when those checkpoints were put, was cut off from their headquarters in Banja Luka; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you think. I think that at that moment Bosnia-Herzegovina was an independent state, and I don't know what the Yugoslav People's Army was doing in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps I will rephrase the question. Isn't it correct that military garrison in Prijedor was cut off and could not have any supplies and traffic with its headquarters in Banja Luka, whichever military label we want to put it on, let's say garrison and soldiers in Banja Luka were cut -- in Prijedor were cut off from Banja Luka by those checkpoints, even if it was one day before the military activities at Kozarac, but that was at least seven days prior?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on that road, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move in another area, and that is the terrible thing that occurred to you, the beating that you received. You have testified yesterday about the nature of the injuries that you have received and you have said that you were attacked with a knife. Could you try to describe or point out the part of the body where you -- that you were stabbed with that knife?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can show it to a doctor without any problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I really didn't mean to be disrespectful. I was just going to try to connect some of the consequences that you have perhaps with the injuries that you received. That could be helpful to you. And it would be helpful to the court, because you said that you were attacked with a knife, and I believe those were the stab injuries, and if you can just say, point with your finger, "I was stabbed here in the chest, I was stabbed here in the back, I was stabbed in the thigh," whatever part of your body, just use the finger and show exactly where were you stabbed?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The knife stabs were on my knee, and the injuries on my head were sustained by blows with a pistol butt. If you were to read my statement closely, you would see what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what part of the arms were injured, and with what weapon?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The left side of the hand, and these three fingers, I think it was -- it came from either rifle butt or a pistol butt. I had protected myself by putting my hand to protect the head and it was broken. I couldn't move these fingers for a month, and I -- I was trying to keep it cool by putting under running water, and I received the first medical assistance when I was in the transit centre in Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you have felt the numbness for long period of time in your hand. Could you just tell us what part of the hand you have felt the numbness in?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, in the fingers. It continues to date. I don't know why I should describe it but, for instance, if I'm trying to turn a screw, I lose strength very quickly, or if I try to use a screwdriver to screw something on, after four or five minutes, I am unable to continue with that, so it -- my hand loses its function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had any surgeries for the injuries that you received on your left hand? Mr. Ryneveld, just the last question and I will connect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, let me hear --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I was just going to ask whether the injuries to this witness are truly in dispute, and if so, why are we dwelling on the consequences to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's a very pertinent question, Mr. Vucicevic, which I have delayed asking you, in order to see --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I was going to ask, the witness has testified that he had numbness, and there was no testimony whether the numbness was immediate, that was permanent, the length of it. And if the stab wound resulted in an injury to the nerve in the arm or that was an injury with a blunt object to an area of the middle, upper arm, or the elbow, either the radial nerve or the ulnar nerve would have been severed and his numbness would have been somewhat different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you seriously disputing the injuries that the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just testing witness' recollection, that's all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead. But let us move quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified earlier that Crdo [phoen] Cirkin, Captain Cirkin, was brought in while you were at Keraterm; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days after you came in he was brought in?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to recall now. Perhaps after ten days or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far back were you in Room 2?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you go down to the -- on the left-hand side, I was at the bottom left corner, that is the first row of pallets to the left at the bottom of the dormitory, so that the door was directly in front of me, so I could see directly through the door when the door was open and I could see the checkpoint at the entrance of Keraterm and so on. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first meet Captain Cirkin?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that was on the eve of the hostilities, on the eve of the attack against Kozarac. He had just returned from the JNA, and we were told that this was Captain Cirkin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it fair to say that you knew him and have seen him more than you have seen Kole before the war, meaning him, Captain Cirkin?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when Captain Cirkin was brought into Room 2 that night, could you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was brought in. I saw him at the entrance. I was not sure whether he was in Room number 2, but I could recognise him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose shift was on duty when Captain Cirkin was brought in, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if a guard came in the same evening to call Captain Cirkin to come out?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that a guard came and that he called him out. I had already pointed that out on one occasion, that he was invited to have something to eat, but he refused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether or not that guard opened the door to look for Captain Cirkin?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who was that guard?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by that time, you were already ten days in the camp? That's correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was about ten days into my stay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the morning, early in the morning, the door was opened up and the guard came again to call Captain Cirkin out; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who was that guard?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that Captain Cirkin came back sometime in the morning, came back to the room? It was daylight. Perhaps you could see him.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever spoken to anybody about such a short stay of Captain Cirkin in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was just a regular talk among the inmates, that he had left the camp the very next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Captain Cirkin is alive and well today, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already testified that he was a commander of defence of Keraterm at that time, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not of Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the one who tried to organise the defence of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it somehow puzzling to you for all the years that have passed, that you, who have only had Motorola and being at the point -- checkpoint at Balte, had stayed for the whole length at Keraterm, while the man who had a command responsibility stayed there one night and was sent elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Vucicevic, reserve your comments for the appropriate stage of the proceedings. Next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you testified -- actually, when you have given a statement to the OTP in three days, from 20th to 22nd of October, 1994, have you signed that document indicating that the statement that you have given is true and correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you read the statement that was in Bosnian before you have signed it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... matters, the facts you have stated therein were true and correct based on your recollection that at that time was only two years old? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if there was a guard whose name was Crni or perhaps a shift commander who was called Crni?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you talked to any of the inmates how many shifts were there just a day or two before you arrived?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we talked about it, that is, we got information, those of us who were brought, that there were three shifts and that they kept rotating all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever had -- ever heard that at some time Tomo Prodan was a shift leader?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you a member of the association of the former inmates of Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not. You can believe it or not, but I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do believe whatever you say, indeed. Have you had a chance to talk to any inmates, either if you had gone back to Bosnia and Herzegovina or in the country where you're at now, about the shifts of all shift leaders that served there, even after you have given this statement?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had occasions even though I think that we tried suppress these stories. We go about our own business. We only recollect on our stay in the camp on occasions, but all of us who live in this country where we live tried to engage in other things, and the camp is something that we --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise for having asked -- asking such a question that jogs your memory. I know that I have talked to more than 50 inmates in my work, and I know how difficult it is, and indeed, you know, on my own, I deeply regret for all that you have suffered, but indeed, we have to do this, and you have been here before, so I think you can appreciate that. The only thing what I call your attention to your previous testimony, and at that time, on page 14, and I am going to read, you're talking about Kole: "I would describe him as about 30 years of age, about 1 metre 75 tall, black hair, medium build, with slouched shoulders and dark complexion."

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How tall are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One eighty-five, 1 metre 85.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Kole is 10 centimetres shorter than you are, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. We didn't stand one -- next to another. This is how I saw -- this is my assessment of his height. But in the camp, we didn't pay attention to how tall someone was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But perhaps 15 centimetres difference between what you said and what his real height is, it's significant, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Especially when there was another shift commander who perfectly fits your description. That's what I'm concerned about.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I have no more questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vucicevic. Before Mr. Ryneveld, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm sorry to rise at the moment. There was a matter which I neglected to put to this witness which I should have done, and I apologise for my neglect. I wonder whether Your Honour would mind if I took about two minutes to put the matter to the witness. I've told my learned friend about this and he has no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. Again I apologise for not having done it before Further cross-examination by Mr. Greaves:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Arifagic, I'll ask you the questions from here. Can you tell me about this: In relation to your departure from Keraterm, when people were selected to go to Omarska, the first time that you have mentioned the name Sikirica in relation to that at all was yesterday? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to make it absolutely plain, you've never mentioned that before. Indeed, when you made your statement in 1994, you said this: "The next day the guards, I do not know who, informed us that some names would be called and we were to gather our belongings and go to a bus. Between 100 and 130 prisoners were called and went to the two or three buses which were parked in the yard at the front of Rooms 1 or 2. I was not called."

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not know the names of anybody who was present on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no other question to ask arising out of that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: One question only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Re-examined by Mr. Ryneveld:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, as a result of Mr. Greaves' questions during cross-examination, you indicated to the court that you had just completed building your house 20 days before the aggression started, and then 20 days later, it burned down. Can you tell us how it burned down or do you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I might be mistaken on this one but, nevertheless, I would like to learn about this procedure. It's my understanding from jurisdiction I'm coming from that redirect could be only asked within the subject of the cross, and this is not -- this wasn't subject of the cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: With respect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: That's where I heard it for the first time. It was on cross. That's why I'm re-examining on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand my question, sir? Would you answer it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My house burned down. That is perhaps one of the proofs that I was not interested in politics and perhaps I was one of the naive people who, on the eve of the war, was still investing the hard-earned money into this family home. It was completely finished and appointed, and with my eight-month-pregnant wife and my daughter, I moved in there. We were putting in new, improved electricity lines, and this happened. Then they ended up in Trnopolje camp together with my father and my mother, and my brother and I ended up in Keraterm. When I first came back, I found only ruins of my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was upon your return from Keraterm that you found your house had burned down; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My first return to Kozarac, the first opportunity that I had to come back to Kozarac, because we had not had opportunity to go there before. I found the ruins and everything had burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Arifagic, that concludes your testimony, and you are discharged.

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, before the next witness is brought in, there is a matter I wanted to raise. It has to do with the motion filed by the Prosecution on the 13th of March for the admission of documentary evidence. This is the second additional request for additional documentary evidence. There has been no response yet from any of the Defence counsel to this motion. When we looked at the motion, however, we saw some elements that required clarification. In the first place, you have submitted several documents, but in respect of those documents, you have expressly stated you are not seeking their admission. And secondly, there is some overlapping between those same documents and the documents whose admission you are in fact seeking. What the Chamber will do is to require you within a week to provide a clarification of those matters and then the Defence counsel will have one week from that clarification to provide any response, if they so wish, and then the 25 Chamber will deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is a witness who testified in the Omarska trial with the protection of a pseudonym and facial distortion. I would ask, Your Honour, that that protection be extended to his testimony in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you provide the basis?

utterances.speaker: MS. BALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we go into private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The witness may be seated. Proceed. We deem that to be sufficiently open. 25 Examined by Ms. Baly:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look, please, at this document that you're about to be shown? Do you see on that document your name written?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And witness do you understand in these proceedings you are going to be referred to as witness G?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BALY
utterances.text: I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed, Ms. Baly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness G, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim, Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As at 1992, did you live in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you completed your schooling in Kozarac, did you complete your compulsory military service in the engineering corps?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And specifically did you work with demolitions?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you finished your military service, did you return to work in the Prijedor area at a firm, a construction company?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that you worked there for 23 years and that you were a crane operator and a mason within the company?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you live in the Kozarusa area?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, may I take you, please, to the 22nd of May, in 1992. Was that, in fact, the last day that you worked at the company?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was my last day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it was a Friday, and you, in fact, did attend work and you travelled to work in your car; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to travel to work, you had to pass through a village known as Orlovci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That village was, at that time, a largely Serb-dominated village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you passed through the village, were you stopped at a checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is -- yes, they stopped me. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that a checkpoint that the Serbs had, in fact, set up some 15 days prior to the 22nd of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it a checkpoint that to your knowledge had been set up 15 days before you passed through it or you arrived at it?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the checkpoint manned by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did some of those soldiers -- were some of those soldiers dressed in what you would call regular army uniform?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they appear to be regular army soldiers with short hair and dressed neatly and wearing clean uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other -- others at the checkpoint who you would describe as being -- looking like Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your understanding, Witness G, of what a Chetnik is?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they wore black fur caps, clothes which were usually of a dark colour, and on those fur caps they had cockades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the checkpoint, was your car searched?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the search were you sent back home?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you notice, Witness G, that the Serbs were, in fact, turning back all cars and buses that had Muslim and Croatian occupants in them?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice that about ten cars and two buses were turned back, and did you also notice that cars with Serbian occupants were allowed to pass through the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you returned home, that is, on the 22nd of May, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the Sunday following the 22nd, that is, on the 24th of May, 1992, was there a report on Radio Prijedor concerning a military convoy?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the report say that the military convoy would pass through Kozarac on its way from Bihac to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it also stated that no one should interfere with the convoy to avoid clashes with the army?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about half past 2.00 that day, did you hear some shooting?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that shooting coming from tanks, anti-aircraft guns, and cannons?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness G, did you in fact see the tanks firing as they were about 300 metres away from your house?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you noticed that the anti-aircraft guns had been placed in position about 15 days prior to the 22nd of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these anti-aircraft guns open fire on hay barns that were in the area?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when the war began, yes, that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you notice that the cannons were in orchards between Orlovci and Prijedor at a place called Kafaniste, which was on the -- and also on the Kozara Mountain?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the shelling -- did the shelling and the firing continue all that day and into the night and through until the following Tuesday at about 11.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And around that time, did a Serbian neighbour of yours who was dressed in an SMB uniform tell you that there was -- that an order had come that you should all attend a certain place?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he describe this place as being a safe place?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of this place?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kozarusa, where the neighbourhood community centre is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from there did he say that buses would, in fact, take you to a safe place?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he also tell you that anyone who did not go would be killed?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it the case, Witness G, that about 2.000 to 3.000 people attended the place, and upon arrival was it the case that the men were immediately separated from the women?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also from the children and the elderly?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think there are about 80 to a hundred people there from where you had come from, from the area where you lived; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were there, I think you were again told that all civilians would be taken to a safe place and that no one would shoot at them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Serbs there also say that they were going to cleanse the forest of Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you understand that to mean, Witness G?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I took it to mean that they would shelter us somewhere until the situation -- until the -- until they resolved the situation, but it simply did not happen that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness G, what did you understand by the expression "cleanse the forest of Green Berets"?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It meant to me that they would look at all our people, Muslims or perhaps other ethnic background, and to cleanse us, that is, put us all into a camp, and that is how we ended up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness G, were you and your family then placed on buses or a bus and taken to the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is, my family to one side and me to the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that when you arrived at the camp, you were separated from -- again, the men were separated from the women and the children and the elderly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For a while, we were separated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you separated for three days, in fact?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice, Witness G, that every day approximately a thousand more people would arrive?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a huge number of people began to flow in a few days after us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And therefore there was not enough room to have the women, children and elderly separated from the men. Is that what took place?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, there was no more room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for that reason, you were all allowed to mingle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, if I understand it well, it seems to me that there is no more room for leading questions because we are coming now to specific particulars which are important for our cross-examination, so I think that the witness should not be led from now on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're right. You will have to -- can't lead any Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 more, Ms. Baly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, for how long did you remain in that -- in the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed in Trnopolje for about 12 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe, please, just very briefly, the conditions in the camp?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conditions were non-existent. We had no water. We had no lavatories. We had no food. They were horrible, to put it simply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness G, in addition to the conditions that you endured, were the detainees mistreated in any way?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a number of instances. A woman was killed, I think the very second day after our arrival there. She was sitting on the school stairs. They simply opened fire from all sides and a stray bullet hit the woman and killed her on those stairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it that opened fire?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Guards opened fire, those who guarded us, those who were around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other instances where detainees were injured or killed in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that point, during those first 12 days of my stay in Trnopolje, people were taken away on a number of occasions, beaten, and then brought back, some bloody and some never came back at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated to the court that you remained in the camp for 12 days. What happened, where were you taken, and where did you go after you left the camp?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Trnopolje, some soldiers looked for me, looked for 23 of us. They found three of us, of those men who they were looking for. They put us on a bus and took us to the barracks in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the other two men that they took to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Redzo Grabic, and Labud Mujkanovic. Labud is a nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnicity is or was Redzo Grabic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the other man?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took us to the barracks in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do those barracks have a name that you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, but it escapes me right now. Is it Zarko Zgonjanin or something? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the barracks used for?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, beforehand, there were army troops in the barracks and armaments in some of the hangars next to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did you remain at those barracks?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some eight or nine days, I'd say, because in those rooms where we were kept, there were no windows, so you couldn't tell day from night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to you on the first day that you arrived at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first day when we arrived in the barracks, we were turned over by the group who escorted us to a group of soldiers, and we were received by Tyson, that was his nickname, and he immediately took us to a small WC, to a small lavatory which was opposite the street. That is, on one side there was the prison, and on the other, I think there were guards, the guards who guarded it. And Tyson there beat all three of us in that small room, in that small lavatory, which was about the area which was about one metre. He beat all three of us there until we all fell one over the other and fainted. And then from a wash basin, which had a hose fixed to it, he sprinkled water on us to make us come back to. And it happened three times. That is, he would beat us and then sprinkle us to bring us back to life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was this person Tyson?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is all I know about him. I know only his nickname, Tyson. I think he was a military policeman. He did have a white belt on his trousers.

utterances.speaker: MS. BALY
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld has just reminded me of the time, Your Honour. Would it be convenient at this time to take a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We will take the break until 2.30. Witness G, during the break, you're not to discuss your evidence with anyone, including the members of the Prosecution team. We are adjourned. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I'm sorry to interrupt in the middle of a witness, but I'm pleased to advise that we have now been provided with French translations of a diagram that have been entered and perhaps we can have those distributed at your convenience, but I just thought you'd like to know that we have those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That's very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: That's for the last witness, Mr. Arifagic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. And in that regard, before we commence with the cross-examination, I'd like to explain of presence of Mr. Pierre Rouve, who -- would you stand so they can see you? Mr. Rouve is not an impostor. He has been provided by the Registrar to the Chamber to assist us in the consultations which the Bench needs to have from time to time, and he will assist in matters of translation and interpretation as required. So if you see him stepping up to the Bench, it's not that the Chamber has a fourth member, I have explained his presence. Where were we in the -- it's Ms. Baly to continue. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness G, before we took the break, you were telling the Court about this person Tyson, and you said that you thought he was a military policeman. Can you -- I ask you why you thought -- why you thought so? Why did you think he was a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing a white belt, which was a sign that he was a member of the military police because the military police always wore white belts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the beating that you received and the spraying down with the hose, were you -- was anything said to you or were you asked any questions?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He only asked of us where we had our weapons, and again, the beating continued. And this was repeated three times. Three times he knocked us unconscious and brought us back to. And then another military policeman came, and he told him to get out of there. He took us to one of the dormitories. It was a real prison because there were metal bars on it, but one could see through, but there was no door. So we had an unobstructed view. There were only bars on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he asked you about the weapons, did you respond?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally said that I did not have any weapons, that the only thing I had was a registered -- a properly registered pistol with the SUP, and I told him where it was, where I had left it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you told him that, did he cease beating you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not stop. He went on, and in the end he told us -- he said, "I'm going to leave for one minute. If you don't say where the weapons were" -- he was going to cut our throats. One minute later, he came back in and then the other military policeman appeared, and he chased him away and put us in this room which was the prison, and he locked us up in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did you remain in that room?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained there for about eight days. There were no windows on it, so I couldn't say whether it was day or night. I was there for seven or eight days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, were you being guarded by anyone in particular?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no specific guard that was guarding us, but the door was locked so nobody could get in. They came to the door and they cursed our balija mothers and provoked us, simply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were "they"?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were soldiers. I think that they were some kind of reservists because they were all a little bit older, 25, 30, 35 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some were wearing olive-drab uniforms, some were wearing camouflage uniforms. And one man stood out. He was always wearing black clothes with a cockade and a long knife he always had on him, 40 to 50 centimetres long. I had never seen Yugoslav army members carrying such knives. Perhaps it was an older type of weapon, maybe something from World War I.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of you were there in that room?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were about eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name the others who were with you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Redzo Grabic, Labud Mujkanovic, then Mirsad Lovic and his son. Then a man called Sengin. Then a man whom they only referred to by the nickname of "machine-gunner." And the two Jakupovic brothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to you while you were in that room?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took me to be interrogated. That was across the way in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kinds of questions were you asked when you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, they asked me to give them my personal data, where I was born, when I was born, when I had done my national service, what branch, whether I was married, how many children I had, where my wife was, where my children were, and they asked me about my brothers, where they were, and other questions -- this is the questions at first. And then they went on to ask me where the weapons were, where the Green Berets were, where do you have lists and who has those lists, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to those latter questions about the Green Berets and the lists and so forth, were you able to answer those questions?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not able to answer them because I was not a part of the Green Berets, nor was I their member, nor did I know about them. I never saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Witness G, who was it that was asking you these questions? Was it the soldiers who you referred to earlier or was it someone else?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing military uniforms, all of them did, but what their duties were, they were probably some officers or members of the Prijedor SUP. They are the ones who were asking questions. I don't know who they were because they only asked questions. All I know is that they were in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what type of uniform were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I remember, the group of those who were asking me questions were -- they were wearing olive-drab uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You referred earlier to Tyson being, you thought, a military -- wearing a military police uniform because of the white belt. Were any of these people who were asking you questions wearing that same white belt?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those men did not have such a belt. I did not notice them having one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After some days, Witness G, did you leave that room, and if so, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several days later, Tyson came in, this other policeman who had brought us there, and he looked like a commander because everybody obeyed him, and told us that we were now going to be going to Keraterm. He put us all in a van, and there was a large black dog in it. He drove us to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just going back for a moment, during these interrogations, did anything -- were you mistreated or -- in any way?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One couldn't say that I was mistreated and abused during the questioning, only -- I only received one kick in leg by one soldier, but it all ended at that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, please, what happened when you arrived at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived at Keraterm, at the entrance, there was -- there were scales and a small hut. That van came and stopped there, and there they took our first and last names and wrote them down. Then the van took us in front of Room 2 and there he told us to get off the van. When we got off, he lined us up alongside a wall. We had to face the wall, place our hands against the wall, and spread our legs. Then Tyson told Zigic that he had four men for special treatment, and at that point, Zigic and several other men started beating us. My -- those of us who were not for special treatment were hit once, maybe twice, it was four of us, but those who were for special treatment were really beaten so badly until they were all covered in blood and until they had fallen down to the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the persons who were for special treatment?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two Jakupovic brothers, Sengin, and a guy whose nickname was "machine-gunner." I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness G, were you ever told what this term "special treatment" meant?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing was said, but we immediately understood, as soon as we arrived at Keraterm. "Special treatment" meant that anybody could beat such a person, kill such a person, do whatever they -- anybody pleased. In fact, this is what happened to the people who were marked for special treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you ever told or given a reason as to why the people were so marked?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one said that, but they were accusing the two Jakupovic brothers that they had raped a young girl. To Sengin they said that he had been a Green Beret. And the one whose nickname was "machine-gunner," they told him that -- about him they were saying that he had a machine-gun, that he was caught with one, and that he was shooting at Serbian children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, Witness G, were you beaten with?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They mostly used rifle butts. Some had some metal pipes and some Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 others had just simply wooden sticks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the beating or, firstly, how long did the beating continue?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It went on. It is hard to say, but perhaps half an hour it lasted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after it finished?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they were done, they told us to go to the room, and they put us in Room 2. And the four who were for special treatment were taken to Room 2 next to the door so that whoever would come, they were always next to the door, available for beating and mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness G, are you able to name any of the participants, the people who actually did the beating?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived at Keraterm, I know that the person who beat me was Zigic, and Duca Knezevic hit me once. But there were other men there, but I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dealing firstly with this person Knezevic, did you know him prior to your arrival at Keraterm, and if so, in what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did know him. I used to see him at the station in Orlovci when I was passing by on the way to work. I would see him there often. And also on the way back, I would also often see him on the bus. We were not friends, but we knew each other. We frequently passed by one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the person Zigic?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Zigic in a similar way as I knew Knezevic. He was a taxi driver, so I would see him at the station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness G, you said you were taken to Room 2. Did you remain in Room 2 for your entire stay at the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not stay there all the time. I stayed there until -- I stayed in Room 2 until my interrogation, and when I was done with interrogation, I was moved to Room 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe briefly, please, what the conditions in Room 2 were like?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Room 2, conditions were very hard. It was a large room and it was overflowing with inmates. We did not have food. We did not have water. You had nothing to wash yourself with. It was too hot. There was no light inside and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any food at all?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were receiving food, one could say, every day once a day. That was in the afternoon, between 3.00 or 5.00 or 6.00 in the afternoon. At any rate, the food was distributed in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the food like?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The food consisted of always two slices of bread. They were machine sliced. That thickness of a slice was 1 to 1.5 centimetres, and there was some kind of a brew, some kind of a soup, sometimes a little bit of potato or some beans or maybe some other food occasionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said earlier that there was no water in the room. Did you receive any water, any -- to drink?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were sometimes getting drinking water. There was a hydrant in Room 4 so that we were able to pour water when we were allowed to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, earlier you also said that you were interrogated during your time in Room 2. Can you please explain to the Court what happened on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I waited in Room number 2 until I was interrogated. When I was -- when I went to be interrogated, a soldier escorted me there. He was escorting people one by one. I arrived in front of the room. I waited a little bit and then a soldier brought me in. There was a soldier standing in the room, and there was another man also military uniform who was sitting at a table and who interrogated us one by one as we were brought in. He was asking questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of questions was he asking?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The questions were when I was born, where I was born, where I had done my military service, where my family was now, did I have brothers, where they were. So that was the start of questioning. Then they moved on to asking questions such as "Where are your weapons?" who was on the Green Beret list, where were Green Berets, and whether I was a Green Beret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you tell them?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was never a member of the Green Berets, that I was never a member of the SDA, that I never had any weapons except for properly registered pistol which I had had for about ten years or less. Before the war had broken out, they had announced on the radio that anybody with weapons should be reported. And I went to the SUP, and they said that I had a properly registered pistol. They said that they were aware of it and if they needed to, they would send someone to collect it because it was a registered weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness G, at night-time did anything happen to the prisoners, and if so, what?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something was happening every night. Some people were taken out, some were killed, and others were beaten up and returned to the rooms. It was a rarity that a night would pass without someone being called out and someone having something done to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to the persons that had been beaten after they'd been beaten?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who were beaten were then taken back to the rooms, and people who were killed would be brought back to the room overnight during the day and then in the evening they would be dumped on a dump. There were debris of tiles and this is where they would be dumped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the detainees who had been beaten receive medical attention?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first I did not observe anyone receiving medical assistance. Later on, when a number of people had been beaten, several men were taken to the hospital. One had his arm broken. One had his head fractured. And they received help. But the others did not get any medical help.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself ever observe a doctor in the camp, and if so, what did you see that doctor doing?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a physician once. I knew him. I think he was a psychiatrist. And he came when one man was killed, to examine him. I knew him from the commission that met for people who were trying to pass a driver's test and he was there to see whether psychologically they were all right. He was an ethnic Macedonian and I think that his last name was Elenkov.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness G, earlier you referred to this person Zigic and also the person Knezevic in the camp beating prisoners. How often did you see them in the camp? And on occasions that you saw them, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a rarity when Zigic and Knezevic were not in Keraterm. Occasionally did happen, but they spent most of their time at Keraterm. And whenever they came to Keraterm, we knew that somebody would either be killed or badly beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any events or is there any event that sticks out in your mind when they did come and beat people?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was one such event. I think that Knezevic's brother or relative or cousin, somebody, was killed, and he came and told us that he had been killed and all of us from Kozarac should then come out from the dormitories, and if somebody failed to do, then he'd better hide well because he would kill him. So all of us, 22 or, I don't know how many, came out. Perhaps there were some from Kozarac who did not come out, I don't know that. And 22 of us were then lined up on pista, in front of Rooms 1 and 2, and they told us to kneel down and then they said that thus on our knees and hands we should head for the gate or rather to that small hut with the weigh bridge. And when we reached it, he then shouted at us to come back. And we had to do it several times. And there was some gravel on the asphalt so that the knees and palms of the hands of the people there were all bloody. And after that, we were ordered to line in two columns, and one opposite the other and to face the other line, and when we turned to face one another, then he ordered us to kneel down. And after we knelt down, then he started, Zigic was behind, and another guy, I don't know his name, walked between these two lines, walked between these two lines, and Zigic picked up a metal rod. And with that rod he hit on the back of the head or the back or wherever, simply wherever he happened to deal that blow, but it was always on the back. And when he hit one, that rod bent because it was a very thin wire, the ones that are used for central heating. And then he ordered a guy to bring a thicker rod, of about two centimetres thick, and with that rod, Zigic then went on beating. He would hit everyone once or twice from the back. And the soldier who walked between the two lines, between two columns, he hit everybody, then he would hit him, and as Zigic would then strike him with this metal rod, his head would come down, and this other one would hit everyone in the face, in the chin, the neck, wherever. I still have a scar here where I was hit, where the tissue was all lacerated and where I bled. Then when Zigic finished that round of beatings, he told us all to stand up, and when we stood up, we again were lined in two columns and facing one another. And he said that now we had to get involved in fighting one another in twosomes, and he said that if we didn't get properly involved, properly committed to such a fight, then he would continue to beat us. And thus group by group started fighting. In that column, I was the last one. I was facing Redzo Grabic, who was my partner, my counterpart. And when the -- my turn came -- when our turn came to engage in a fight, Kajin arrived from the weigh bridge and told Zigic to stop it.
